thread:
Evan: Heads up — found a surprising behavior in the Go SDK generator around connection resets + immediate retry + context deadlines. Copying notes here so we can decide a recommended pattern.

Harper: TL;DR?

Evan: When a TCP reset happens during the HTTP/2 handshake while streaming, the first Generate() returns an error. If the caller retries immediately with the same request and a fresh context, sometimes the server-side reports duplicate partial outputs (server sees fragments re-played). Locally I can reproduce by simulating a mid-handshake RST.

Nadia: Does this only happen with reused Generator vs new one?

Evan: Mostly when we reuse the same Generator client and same underlying transport. Workaround: create a new Generator (or new underlying transport) for the retry. That forces a clean handshake and avoids replay.

Harper: Can you share the minimal repro code?

Evan: Sure, simplified snippet:
```go
// caller code (simplified)
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()
iter, err := gen.Generate(ctx, req)
if err != nil {
  // immediate retry
  ctx2, cancel2 := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
  defer cancel2()
  iter2, err2 := gen.Generate(ctx2, req)
  return handle(iter2, err2)
}
return handle(iter, err)
```
Repro uses a proxy that drops the TLS stream mid-handshake.

Nadia: Thanks. Observations from runtime: the transport has an internal buffer for pre-handshake frames; when the reset happens, some bytes remain in the socket buffer and get associated with the next connection because OS/TCP stack can hand them to the new socket in weird proxy setups.

Harper: Good catch. We probably need two things: (1) SDK guidance in docs (recommended: new Generator/transport on retry for critical idempotent workflows); (2) add an optional transport-level resetOnRetry flag that closes file descriptors and clears buffers between attempts.

Evan: I prototyped Transport.WithResetOnRetry(true) in a fork. It forces a small delay, closes the underlying net.Conn and re-dials. Reduced repro rate to ~1%. Downside: extra latency on retries.

Nadia: Another angle: make Generate accept a RetryPolicy that indicates whether the SDK should force a fresh transport, or reuse. That lets users trade cost/latency for safety.

Harper: We should add a sample to quickstart that demonstrates safe retry patterns and shows the generator-per-retry cost/latency tradeoff. Also call out that mobile networks and flaky proxies can cause RST/replay.

Evan: Created a tiny test harness and a gist with the proxy script. Filing issue and PR with sample + docs.

CI-bot: Issue created: #5062 "go-sdk: connection-reset leads to partial replay on immediate retry". PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/245 (ci: linux/amd64 flaky)

Harper: Assigning to eng-runtime and devex to triage. Recommend adding a short note to the streaming FAQ in the meantime.

Nadia: I can help review the transport API shape. Also propose we add a non-blocking Iterator.Close(context) to let callers abort safely without waiting on Result().

Evan: Added both in the PR: RetryPolicy + Iterator.Close(ctx). Tests included. Will ping for review.

Harper: Thanks. Once merged, we should update the Go quickstart and include a small section in the SDK migration notes about context/handshake gotchas.

Evan: Will do — closing this thread after PR lands. Thanks for the quick feedback :rocket:
